text:
Quinn Hughes is the most talked-about defenseman in hockey for a reason that has nothing to do with his points. The Star Tribune ran a column headlined "We love your game, Quinn Hughes. Now make up your mind," and Elliotte Friedman's updates on his future keep circulating. On the ice, he's answering a different question: 30 points in 22 games, an 11-game point streak, and his ice time up 2:15 a night to 29:17 over his last ten.

Minnesota controls 57.5% of the expected goals at five on five with him, 10 points better than without him. That part is real. The goals are the soft spot: seven on 3.8 expected, shooting 12% after 4% last season. Our form read calls the last ten games mostly bounces, so expect fewer goals and the same playmaking.

Evolving-Hockey had him first among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his shot assists in the 99th percentile. Watch the minutes. A coach leaning on him this hard is telling you something.
headline: Quinn Hughes is playing 29 minutes and every one counts
